heading: EXT. TIDAL-LOCKED STATION - TERMINATOR RAIL - ETERNAL DUSK

units.text: EXT. TIDAL-LOCKED STATION - TERMINATOR RAIL - ETERNAL DUSK
A single rail hangs between night and day.
On one horizon the sun is a thin white edge.
On the other, stars.
The station crawls along the track, a lit tube no wider than a bus.
Inside the observation cab, four figures strap into acceleration couches.
Outside, nothing moves.
YUSUF BARANOWSKI, 50s, grey-haired, runs a gloved finger along a dead console.
He mutters a number and moves on.
FREYA ODUYA, 30s, beside him, tightens a harness strap, loosens it again, tightens it.
She stops when he looks.
MARCELINE VOSS, 20s, near the porthole, presses her forehead to the glass.
Her breath fogs it.
DAGMAR NYONI, 40s, at the rear, checks the oxygen gauge for the fourth time.
The station shudders.
A thud rolls through the floor.
They all grab for something.
He reaches across and clamps her hand on the strap.
She nods.
They both stare at the porthole as the rail ahead begins to buckle.
She curses.
He swallows.
They share a glance, nothing in it.
Rail's flexing.
units.name: YUSUF

units.text: Expected.
units.name: FREYA

units.text: It's never flexed that much.
units.name: MARCELINE

units.text: It's within tolerance.
units.name: DAGMAR

units.text: The cab rocks.
Marceline's knuckles whiten on the rim.
Behind her, Dagmar unstraps, crosses, puts both hands on the girl's shoulders.
Marceline doesn't look back.
The rail steadies.
The glow along the horizon holds.
Yusuf lets his breath out.
Freya gives a short, tight laugh.
The four of them sit in the hum of the engines, watching the sun not rise.
